### src/app/LogLuts.cpp
```
// LogLuts.cpp -- see LogLuts.h.

#include "app/LogLuts.h"

#ifdef SS_TOOL_SFM
#include "sfm/core/Telemetry.h"
#endif

#include <algorithm>
#include <cmath>

namespace app {

namespace {

enum class LogCurve { SLog3, VLog, FLog, FLog2, DLog, ILog, CanonLog3, NLog, GpLog, GpLog2 };
// Fitted: m2 * curve_w(m1 * lin) + black, each of the kLogMixes mixes through
// its own monotone curve. Bt709: GoPro's technical LUT, m2 * OETF(lin). GpLog2:
// GoPro Labs' GP-Log2 generator.
enum class LogLook { Fitted, Bt709, GpLog2 };

constexpr int kLogLutSize = 33, kLogMixes = 6;
// Curve knots one stop apart, the first at 2^kLogKnot0 times 18% grey.
constexpr int kLogKnot0 = -8, kLogKnots = 15;

struct LogLutParams {
    BuiltinLut lut;
    LogCurve curve;
    LogLook look;
    double to709[9];  // the camera's gamut to linear Rec.709, row-major
    double m1[kLogMixes * 3], m2[3 * kLogMixes];
    double knots[kLogMixes * kLogKnots];
    double black[3];  // the look's lifted black, display code
};

}  // namespace
}  // namespace app

#include "app/LogLutTable.h"

namespace app {

namespace {

// The makers' published curves, code value / 1023 to scene linear with 18%
// grey at 0.18 -- GoPro's with 1 at clip. tools/fit_log_luts.py decode() cites
// each source and must agree with this one.
double decode(LogCurve c, double x) {
    switch (c) {
    case LogCurve::SLog3: {
        const double v = x * 1023;
        return v >= 171.2102946929 ? std::pow(10.0, (v - 420) / 261.5) * 0.19 - 0.01
                                   : (v - 95) * 0.01125 / (171.2102946929 - 95);
    }
    case LogCurve::VLog:
        return x < 0.181 ? (x - 0.125) / 5.6 : std::pow(10.0, (x - 0.598206) / 0.241514) - 0.00873;
    case LogCurve::FLog:
        return x < 0.100537775223865 ? (x - 0.092864) / 8.735631
                                     : (std::pow(10.0, (x - 0.790453) / 0.344676) - 0.009468) / 0.555556;
    case LogCurve::FLog2:
        return x < 0.100686685370811 ? (x - 0.092864) / 8.799461
                                     : (std::pow(10.0, (x - 0.384316) / 0.245281) - 0.064829) / 5.555556;
    case LogCurve::DLog:
        return x <= 0.14 ? (x - 0.0929) / 6.025
                         : (std::pow(10.0, 3.89616 * x - 2.27752) - 0.0108) / 0.9892;
    case LogCurve::ILog:
        return x < 0.154402 ? (x - 0.09055934) / 5.77837328
                            : std::pow(10.0, (x - 0.623992) / 0.280055) - 0.01;
    case LogCurve::CanonLog3: {
        const double t = (x * 1023 - 64) / 876;  // Canon Log 3 is defined on legal range
        const double v = t < 0.04076162 ? -(std::pow(10.0, (0.07623209 - t) / 0.42889912) - 1) / 14.98325
                         : t <= 0.105357102 ? (t - 0.073059361) / 2.3069815
                                            : (std::pow(10.0, (t - 0.069886632) / 0.42889912) - 1) / 14.98325;
        return 0.9 * v;
    }
    case LogCurve::NLog: {
        const double t = x / (650.0 / 1023);
        return x < 452.0 / 1023 ? t * t * t - 0.0075 : std::exp((x - 619.0 / 1023) / (150.0 / 1023));
    }
    case LogCurve::GpLog: return (std::pow(400.0, x) - 1) / 399;
    case LogCurve::GpLog2: return (std::pow(600.0, x) - 1) / 599;
    }
    return 0;
}

double oetf709(double v) {
    v = std::max(v, 0.0);
    return v < 0.018 ? 4.5 * v : 1.099 * std::pow(std::max(v, 0.018), 0.45) - 0.099;
}

// Fritsch-Butland slopes on unit-spaced, rising knots -- SciPy's PCHIP.
void pchip_slopes(const double* y, double* m) {
    double d[kLogKnots - 1];
    for (int k = 0; k + 1 < kLogKnots; k++) d[k] = y[k + 1] - y[k];
    for (int k = 1; k + 1 < kLogKnots; k++)
        m[k] = d[k - 1] * d[k] > 0 ? 2 * d[k - 1] * d[k] / (d[k - 1] + d[k] + 1e-300) : 0.0;
    auto edge = [](double d0, double d1) {
        const double e = (3 * d0 - d1) / 2;
        if (e * d0 <= 0) return 0.0;
        return d0 * d1 <= 0 && std::fabs(e) > 3 * std::fabs(d0) ? 3 * d0 : e;
    };
    m[0] = edge(d[0], d[1]);
    m[kLogKnots - 1] = edge(d[kLogKnots - 2], d[kLogKnots - 3]);
}

// Hermite between the knots on a log2 axis; linear in x to 0 below the first,
// flat past the last.
double curve(const double* y, const double* m, double x) {
    const double u = std::log2(std::max(x, 1e-30) / 0.18) - kLogKnot0;
    if (u <= 0) return y[0] * std::max(x, 0.0) / (0.18 * std::exp2(kLogKnot0));
    if (u >= kLogKnots - 1) return y[kLogKnots - 1];
    const int k = std::min((int)u, kLogKnots - 2);
    const double t = u - k, t2 = t * t, t3 = t2 * t;
    return (2 * t3 - 3 * t2 + 1) * y[k] + (t3 - 2 * t2 + t) * m[k] + (3 * t2 - 2 * t3) * y[k + 1] +
           (t3 - t2) * m[k + 1];
}

// GoPro Labs' GP-Log2 LUT generator (gopro.github.io/labs/gplog2, Apache-2.0;
// LICENSES/Apache-2.0-GoPro-Labs.txt) at its defaults: +1.8 EV, then its
// highlight rolloff, then the BT.709 OETF.
double gplog2_rolloff(double x, double max_in) {
    const double start = 0.25, end_slope = 0.01;
    if (x <= start) return x;
    if (x >= max_in) return 1.0;
    const double dx = max_in - start, avg = (1.0 - start) / dx;
    if (avg <= end_slope || avg >= 1.0) return x;
    const double p = (1.0 - end_slope) / (avg - end_slope) - 1.0, t = (x - start) / dx;
    return start + dx * (end_slope * t + (1.0 - end_slope) * (1.0 - std::pow(1.0 - t, p + 1.0)) / (p + 1.0));
}

double gplog2_toe(double v) {
    const double above = 1.0, maximum = 1.4, inv = 1 / (maximum - above);
    const double gain = (1.2 - above) / (maximum - above);
    const double n = 1 - v;
    if (n <= above) return v;
    const double a = std::min(1.0, n * inv);
    return 1 - ((n - above) * (a * gain + (1 - a)) + above);
}

void map(const LogLutParams& p, const double* slopes, const double code[3], float out[3]) {
    double cam[3], lin[3], v[3] = {p.black[0], p.black[1], p.black[2]};
    for (int c = 0; c < 3; c++) cam[c] = decode(p.curve, code[c]);
    for (int c = 0; c < 3; c++)
        lin[c] = p.to709[3 * c] * cam[0] + p.to709[3 * c + 1] * cam[1] + p.to709[3 * c + 2] * cam[2];
    switch (p.look) {
    case LogLook::Fitted:
        for (int w = 0; w < kLogMixes; w++) {
            const double x = p.m1[3 * w] * lin[0] + p.m1[3 * w + 1] * lin[1] + p.m1[3 * w + 2] * lin[2];
            const double y = curve(p.knots + w * kLogKnots, slopes + w * kLogKnots, x);
            for (int c = 0; c < 3; c++) v[c] += p.m2[c * kLogMixes + w] * y;
        }
        break;
    case LogLook::Bt709:
        for (int c = 0; c < 3; c++)
            for (int j = 0; j < 3; j++) v[c] += p.m2[c * kLogMixes + j] * oetf709(lin[j]);
        break;
    case LogLook::GpLog2: {
        const double gain = std::pow(2.0, 1.8);
        for (int c = 0; c < 3; c++) v[c] = oetf709(gplog2_toe(gplog2_rolloff(lin[c] * gain, gain)));
        break;
    }
    }
    for (int c = 0; c < 3; c++) out[c] = (float)std::clamp(v[c], 0.0, 1.0);
}

const LogLutParams* find_params(const std::string& id) {
    for (const LogLutParams& p : kLogLuts)
        if (id == p.lut.id) return &p;
    return nullptr;
}

}  // namespace

const std::vector<BuiltinLut>& builtin_luts() {
    static const std::vector<BuiltinLut> luts = [] {
        std::vector<BuiltinLut> v;
        for (const LogLutParams& p : kLogLuts) v.push_back(p.lut);
        return v;
    }();
    return luts;
}

const BuiltinLut* find_builtin_lut(const std::string& id) {
    for (const BuiltinLut& b : builtin_luts())
        if (id == b.id) return &b;
    return nullptr;
}

std::string detect_log_lut(const std::string& video) {
#ifdef SS_TOOL_SFM
    const sfm::VideoLogProfile p = sfm::video_log_profile(video);
    // DJI ships one D-Log M LUT for most of its cameras and a second for the
    // 2025 ones; the Avata 360 (wa530) is among those.
    const bool dji_2025 =
        p.camera == "dvtm_AVATA360.proto" || p.camera == "dvtm_eagle4_wa530.proto";
    const char* id = p.log == "dji-d-log-m" ? (dji_2025 ? "dji-dlog-m-2025" : "dji-dlog-m")
                     : p.log == "dji-d-log"   ? "dji-dlog"
                     : p.log == "gp-log"      ? "gopro-gplog"
                     : p.log == "s-log3-cine" ? "sony-slog3"
                     : p.log == "v-log"       ? "panasonic-vlog"
                                              : nullptr;
    if (id && find_builtin_lut(id)) return builtin_lut_spec(id);
#else
    (void)video;
#endif
    return {};
}

bool bake_builtin_lut(const std::string& id, CubeLut& out, std::string& error) {
    const LogLutParams* p = find_params(id);
    if (!p) {
        error = "no built-in LUT named " + id;
        return false;
    }
    double slopes[kLogMixes * kLogKnots];
    for (int w = 0; w < kLogMixes; w++) pchip_slopes(p->knots + w * kLogKnots, slopes + w * kLogKnots);
    const int n = kLogLutSize;
    out = CubeLut();
    out.size = n;
    out.title = p->lut.name;
    out.rgb.resize((size_t)n * n * n * 3);
    float* o = out.rgb.data();
    for (int b = 0; b < n; b++)
        for (int g = 0; g < n; g++)
            for (int r = 0; r < n; r++, o += 3) {
                const double code[3] = {(double)r / (n - 1), (double)g / (n - 1), (double)b / (n - 1)};
                map(*p, slopes, code, o);
            }
    return true;
}

}  // namespace app
```

### src/app/LogLuts.h

#pragma once

// The log -> Rec.709 LUTs Spirula knows without a file: each maker's published
// log curve and gamut, then a look -- fitted by tools/fit_log_luts.py to how the
// maker's own LUT renders natural photographs, or GoPro's exact formulas --
// baked to a lattice the first time a run asks for one. docs/notes/log-luts.md.

#include "app/CubeLut.h"

#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace app {

struct BuiltinLut {
    const char* id;    // what builtin_lut_spec() and --lut name
    const char* name;  // the maker's own name for the profile, untranslated
};

const std::vector<BuiltinLut>& builtin_luts();
const BuiltinLut* find_builtin_lut(const std::string& id);
// Its lattice; false with `error` set for an unknown id.
bool bake_builtin_lut(const std::string& id, CubeLut& out, std::string& error);

// The built-in a clip's own metadata says it was recorded for, as a spec; ""
// when it names none -- which includes every clip that was not shot in log.
std::string detect_log_lut(const std::string& video);

}  // namespace app

### src/app/Main.cpp
```
// The one entry point -- see app/Tools.h for why there is only one. The
// subcommands are the tools() table below; `spirula` alone is the window, and
// `spirula <file-or-folder>` is the window opening what was named.
//
// A first argument that is not a subcommand goes to the GUI untouched, so
// "Open with" from a file manager and a shell alias both land on the right
// screen. On a build with no GUI it is an error naming the subcommands, which
// is the only thing such a build can do.

#include "app/AppPaths.h"
#include "app/CrashLog.h"
#include "app/Tools.h"
#include "i18n/Locale.h"
#include "i18n/catalog/Cli.h"
#include "i18n/catalog/Dense.h"
#ifdef SS_HAVE_LPIPS
#include "app/EvalLpips.h"
#endif
#ifdef SS_TOOL_SAM
#include "app/ModelLicenses.h"
#include "app/cli/LicenseCli.h"   // --accept-license: the inference layer is in this build
#include "nn/Device.h"
#endif

#include <cctype>
#include <exception>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#ifdef _WIN32
#include <io.h>
#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#include <windows.h>   // NOMINMAX comes from cmake/SsOptions.cmake
#define isatty _isatty
#define fileno _fileno
#else
#include <unistd.h>
#endif
#include <cstring>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace {

namespace cmsg = spirula::i18n::msg::cli;

#ifdef _WIN32
UINT g_console_cp = 0;

// A console keeps a code page of its own, which src/app/utf8.manifest does not
// touch: every CJK path this prints into a cp437 window would be mojibake.
// Restored at exit, because cmd.exe keeps whatever code page it is left with.
void use_utf8_console() {
    const UINT prev = GetConsoleOutputCP();
    if (prev == 0 || prev == CP_UTF8 || !SetConsoleOutputCP(CP_UTF8)) return;
    g_console_cp = prev;
    std::atexit([] { SetConsoleOutputCP(g_console_cp); });
}
#endif

// The subcommand NAME is an identifier and prints as it is written; the
// summary is a message, so `spirula --help` follows --lang like everything
// else. It is a pointer rather than a copy because a Msg is immortal .rodata
// and the language may change under it (it cannot here, but the habit is what
// keeps a cached `const char*` from ever appearing).
struct Tool {
    const char* name;
    const spirula::i18n::Msg* summary;
    int (*run)(int, char**);
};

const std::vector<Tool>& tools() {
    static const std::vector<Tool> kTools = {
#ifdef SS_TOOL_GUI
        {app::kToolGui, &cmsg::tool_gui, spirula_gui_main},
#endif
#ifdef SS_TOOL_SFM
        {app::kToolSfm, &cmsg::tool_sfm, spirula_sfm_main},
#endif
#ifdef SS_TOOL_TRAIN
        {app::kToolTrain, &cmsg::tool_train, spirula_train_main},
#endif
#ifdef SS_TOOL_SAM
        {app::kToolSam, &cmsg::tool_sam, spirula_sam_main},
#endif
#ifdef SS_TOOL_GEOMETRY
        {app::kToolGeometry, &cmsg::tool_geometry, spirula_geometry_main},
#endif
#ifdef SS_TOOL_DENSE
        {app::kToolDense, &spirula::i18n::msg::dense::title, spirula_dense_main},
#endif
#ifdef SS_TOOL_MESH
        {app::kToolMesh, &cmsg::tool_mesh, spirula_mesh_main},
#endif
#ifdef SS_TOOL_E57
        {app::kToolE57, &cmsg::tool_e57, spirula_e57_main},
        {app::kToolLidar, &cmsg::tool_lidar, spirula_lidar_main},
#endif
#ifdef SS_TOOL_ENCODE
        {app::kToolEncode, &cmsg::tool_encode, spirula_encode_main},
#endif
#ifdef SS_TOOL_PARTITION
        {app::kToolPartition, &cmsg::tool_partition, spirula_partition_main},
#endif
#ifdef SS_TOOL_MARKER
        {app::kToolMarker, &cmsg::tool_marker, spirula_marker_main},
#endif
    };
    return kTools;
}

const Tool* find_tool(const char* name) {
    if (!name) return nullptr;
    for (const Tool& t : tools())
        if (std::strcmp(t.name, name) == 0) return &t;
    return nullptr;
}

// argv[0] as a tool name: a copy or symlink called spirula-sfm runs the SfM
// tool, which is how the separately-named executables of earlier releases keep
// working. Only the basename matters, and only the part after the prefix.
// "ssplat-" is the pre-rename spelling and still resolves.
const Tool* tool_from_argv0(const char* argv0) {
    if (!argv0) return nullptr;
    std::string s = argv0;
    const size_t slash = s.find_last_of("/\\");
    if (slash != std::string::npos) s = s.substr(slash + 1);
    for (char& c : s) c = (char)std::tolower((unsigned char)c);
    if (s.size() > 4 && s.compare(s.size() - 4, 4, ".exe") == 0)
        s.resize(s.size() - 4);
    for (const char* prefix : {"spirula-", "ssplat-"})
        if (s.rfind(prefix, 0) == 0)
            return find_tool(s.c_str() + std::strlen(prefix));
    return nullptr;
}

void print_usage() {
    std::printf("Spirula Studio " SS_VERSION "\n\n");
#ifdef SS_TOOL_GUI
    std::printf("  spirula                        %s\n",
                cmsg::usage_open_app.get());
    std::printf("  spirula <file-or-folder>       %s\n",
                cmsg::usage_open_target.get());
#endif
    std::printf("  spirula <command> [options]\n\n");
    std::printf("%s\n", cmsg::usage_commands.get());
    for (const Tool& t : tools())
        std::printf("  %-8s %s\n", t.name, t.summary->get());
    std::printf("\n%s\n", cmsg::usage_per_command_help.get());
    std::printf("\n%s\n\n%s", cmsg::usage_lang.get(),
                spirula::i18n::language_list().c_str());
}

// The inference device must go before static destructors run: a validation
// layer's own statics are gone by then, and it aborts on the first call.
int finish_tool(int rc) {
#ifdef SS_TOOL_SAM
    nn::shutdown();
#endif
    return rc;
}

}  // namespace

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
#ifdef __APPLE__
    // macOS 26 kills a long GPU command buffer the window server is waiting on
    // ("Impacting Interactivity"). Apple's GPU driver reads this when the first
    // Metal device opens; children inherit it, and a value already set is kept.
    setenv("AGX_RELAX_CDM_CTXSTORE_TIMEOUT", "1", 0);
#endif
    // Stop FULL buffering of stdout whenever it is NOT a terminal. Every tool
    // here is routinely run as a CHILD PROCESS with its output piped to a live
    // log -- the GUI does it for reconstruction, masking and meshing -- and the
    // C runtime's default for a pipe is full buffering, which holds 4 KB of
    // progress back until the buffer fills or the process exits. A run that
    // prints one line a minute then appears to print nothing at all for the
    // first hour, which is exactly the failure it looks like.
    //
    // The two runtimes need different modes for the same result, and the
    // Windows one is unforgiving about both halves:
    //   * its CRT has no line buffering at all -- `_IOLBF` is documented to be
    //     treated as `_IOFBF` -- so asking for it would leave the stall in
    //     place;
    //   * and it rejects a zero size for the buffered modes, through an
    //     invalid-parameter handler that is `__fastfail`. The process then dies
    //     at this line with status 0xC0000409 and NOTHING on either stream --
    //     which reads, from the parent, as a tool that failed instantly for no
    //     reason. Only `_IONBF` is allowed a zero size there.
    if (!isatty(fileno(stdout))) {
#ifdef _WIN32
        std::setvbuf(stdout, nullptr, _IONBF, 0);
#else
        std::setvbuf(stdout, nullptr, _IOLBF, 0);
#endif
    }
#ifdef _WIN32
    use_utf8_console();
#endif

    // --lang is handled here and removed from argv, so no tool's own parser
    // has to know about it. The chain that decides the language is in
    // src/i18n/Locale.h; the GUI re-runs it once it has read its settings
    // file, which is a step below --lang and the environment.
    const char* lang = spirula::i18n::take_lang_arg(&argc, argv);
    spirula::i18n::init(lang, nullptr);

#ifdef SS_TOOL_SAM
    // --accept-license, anywhere in argv and for every command: how a terminal
    // accepts a model licence. Removed from argv, so no tool's parser sees it;
    // the gate installed here answers every command that fetches a licensed model.
    try {
        app::register_model_licenses();
        app::install_license_gate();
        app::consume_accept_license_args(argc, argv);
    } catch (const std::exception& e) {
        std::fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", e.what());
        return 2;
    }
#endif
#ifdef SS_HAVE_LPIPS
    spirula::install_eval_lpips();
#endif

    // Every tool, not only the window: the GUI runs reconstruction, masking
    // and meshing as child processes, and a child that dies of a fault leaves
    // its parent an exit status and nothing else.
    app::install_crash_log(app::config_dir());

    // An explicit subcommand wins over the argv[0] hint, so a binary that was
    // renamed or symlinked still answers to every tool it holds. No subcommand
    // name collides with an argument any of them takes, so `spirula-sfm auto`
    // falls through to the name check below and reaches the SfM tool.
    if (argc > 1) {
        if (const Tool* t = find_tool(argv[1])) {
            // The tool sees "spirula sfm" as its program name, so its own usage
            // text prints a command line that can be pasted back.
            std::string prog = std::string(argv[0] ? argv[0] : "spirula") + " " + t->name;
            app::set_crash_note(prog);
            std::vector<char*> sub;
            sub.push_back(prog.data());
            for (int i = 2; i < argc; i++) sub.push_back(argv[i]);
            sub.push_back(nullptr);
            return finish_tool(t->run((int)sub.size() - 1, sub.data()));
        }
    }

    // Named as a tool: hand it everything, --help and --version included, so a
    // spirula-sfm symlink behaves exactly as the separate executable did.
    if (const Tool* t = tool_from_argv0(argc > 0 ? argv[0] : nullptr)) {
        app::set_crash_note(t->name);
        return finish_tool(t->run(argc, argv));
    }

    if (argc > 1) {
        const std::string a = argv[1];
        if (a == "help" || a == "--help" || a == "-h") {
            print_usage();
            return 0;
        }
        if (a == "--version" || a == "-v") {
            std::printf("%s\n", SS_VERSION);
            return 0;
        }
    }

#ifdef SS_TOOL_GUI
    return spirula_gui_main(argc, argv);
#else
    if (argc > 1)
        std::fprintf(stderr, "%s\n\n",
                     spirula::i18n::format(cmsg::err_unknown_command,
                                           {argv[1]}).c_str());
    else
        std::fprintf(stderr, "%s\n\n", cmsg::err_no_gui.get());
    print_usage();
    return 2;
#endif
}
```
